notes.title: Devblog - There are more characters than planned!
notes.notes:
Hooray, friends! The game has entered the closed beta stage!
And I have some news for you!

A lot has changed since the release of the first alpha, both in gameplay and graphics. We've added more details, decorations, various additional animations, replaced some character textures, and much more!
I even managed to tweak the camera behavior, making it smoother and more enjoyable for the players.

But sometimes, I get carried away and do a bit more than originally planned. This time, it happened with the characters... or rather, their number 😅
The thing is, the game was initially planned to have a fixed number of characters, which could only be unlocked as you progress through the story. However, at some point in the middle of the alpha development process, the game ended up with an additional page of characters. And I couldn’t fit them into the storyline... So I started looking for solutions, but rather lazily 😛. Meanwhile, I kept coming up with new characters I wanted to add as playable ones. And now, there’s already a fourth page of characters... Yes, the game will now feature 20 playable characters—10 story-based and 10 additional ones.
As for the additional characters, you’ll be able to unlock them by finding their cards. Many of these cards will be located in various places, often in plain sight, but some of them might be easy to miss! So don’t forget, exploration is always rewarded in the genre of my game!

See you at the release, adventurers!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45279339/8a38269917ce77e9d125644e7d8acd3c1e5240a8.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Devblog - About the Interface from the Old Alpha Versions and the New Ones
notes.notes:
How the character selection menu interface has evolved since the first alpha versions.

At first, I wanted the interface to resemble the one from Painted Legend 2, where there was more information about the character and their abilities, and the character buttons were just pieces of paper with their names. However, I soon realized that the icons from the very first game were more colorful and appealing due to the portraits of the selectable characters. So, I decided to redesign the menu to include both the character icons and their abilities simultaneously.

Everything was great, but I still didn’t like how the portraits in the first game were very small, which wouldn’t work for the new game. So, I decided to split the character buttons into groups of 5 per page and allow scrolling left and right to fit larger portraits on the screen :)
